Oral Order 05/Dated: 12.02.2024 Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioner in this writ application has made the following prayers:-
"For issuance of an appropriate writ (s)/order(s)/direction(s) in the nature of mandamus directing the Respondents to pay compensation for acquisition of land of Khata no. 26, Plot no. 235 and Khata no. 35, Plot no. 375 of Thana no. 206 of Area 1.86 acres of Village Dinadag, Chhatarpur, as aforesaid land has been acquired for construction of National Highway 98 from kilometer 23.84 Hariharganj to K.M. 57.049 Pandwa, as Respondents are paying compensation to other raiyats of the same mouza."
It is the case of the petitioner that the land, which was acquired and used by the National Highway Authority of India, was settled in favour of the ancestor of this petitioner.
Thereafter, the petitioner is in possession over the land and is entitled to receive the compensation.

sentences.text: 1 respondents have not paid the compensation in lieu of acquisition, thus the Respondents have committed gross illegality.

Learned counsel for the State submits that since the land is 'gair mazarua aam' land, the State has transferred the land in favour of NHAI and the petitioner is not entitled to receive any amount of compensation.
From the submissions of the parties, I find that there is a serious dispute in respect of the ownership over the land in question.

The petitioner claims that the land was settled in favour of the ancestors,
for which Register II was also opened in the name of the ancestors and they are paying rent.
On the other hand, the State is claiming title over the land in question.
Section 3 H of the National Highways Act provides for resolution of dispute in these type of situations.

It is necessary to quote Section 3 H (3) and (4) of the National Highways Act, which reads as under:-
"3H. Deposit and payment of amount.--

(3) Where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

(4) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated."

Thus, from the aforesaid provision, it is clear that the Competent Authority, who, in this case is the District Land Acquisition Officer can take an appropriate decision either to determine as to who is to receive the compensation or if there is any dispute, refer the matter to the principal civil court,
having original jurisdiction.

Considering the aforesaid provision of the NHA Act, I direct the petitioner to approach the Competent Authority i.e. the District Land Acquisition Officer by raising his grievance by annexing all the documents, which the petitioner is relying upon.

Once the documents are filed, the Competent Authority will hear the petitioner and will take an appropriate decision either to invoke the section 3 H (3) or section 3 H (4) of the aforesaid Act and proceed accordingly.
The entire process should be concluded within a period of twelve weeks from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, this writ petition stands disposed of.

(Ananda Sen, J.) APK Vijay Prajapati vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23153745/
